feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior-level CV with clear positioning, credible scope, and relevant public-sector digital leadership experience. It reads polished and substantive, but it is slightly repetitive across sections and could be tightened to improve scannability and sharpen impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear executive profile: the headline and summary immediately establish a strong niche in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and communications systems.  
- Good credibility signals: large-scale metrics (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) and progression within NACo strengthen seniority and trust.  
- Broad but coherent skill set: strategy, technical execution, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are well aligned with the target brand.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to save space and make the CV easier to scan.  
- Add more outcome-focused results: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more quantified business/user outcomes would increase impact (e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption improvements).  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak/irrelevant filler; capitalization/style varies slightly across sections (“AI-enabled,” “front-end,” “organization-wide”). No major misspellings or grammar errors otherwise.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one sharper value proposition and a few concrete signals of scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and make more specific: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years leading public-sector web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume, mission-driven organizations.”
- Add scale or scope already evidenced in the CV, e.g. “enterprise websites,” “10,000+ page platforms,” or “multi-channel communications ecosystems.”
- Replace “Leads” with a parallel noun-based structure for smoother style: “Expertise spans enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial governance, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search/content experiences.”
- Consider aligning wording more closely with the subtitle to avoid sounding repetitive while reinforcing your niche.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” substantially repeats the subtitle and Core Competencies.
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with recent projects; “AI-enabled search and content experiences” would be more precise.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the headline, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinct will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, concise noun phrases and remove softer wording like “operations” where possible.
- Reorder to emphasize most senior/recent strengths first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search, automation.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestreaming
- Standardize style: spell out “and” instead of “&” if used elsewhere in section headers/body copy.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “digital governance,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled search” repeat the header and Topline Skills almost verbatim.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is also duplicated in Topline Skills and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing outcomes, scope, or distinct formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use stronger, more specific verbs and cleaner lists: “combined hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content, and bill-level AI chat.”
- Clarify unique value or audience impact where possible: campaign growth, policy discovery, member engagement, conference activation.
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency and readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- If this footer stays, position these as “selected projects” with distinct outcomes or formats not already described elsewhere.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and Recent Projects. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add scope/results where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded full-time as a strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, campaigns, content operations, and AI-enabled search.”
- Consolidate execution bullets: combine “digital systems, workflows and analytics” with “governance, usability and operational best practices” into one outcome-focused bullet.
- Make the Drupal/campaign bullet more specific: mention number of microsites, toolkit launches, or audience/member reach if available.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: site scale, publishing volume, time saved, search/discovery improvements, stakeholder adoption, or performance gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI-enabled search, microsites, and anniversary/campaign work are already echoed in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “enterprise web improvement” also repeat the summary and prior NACo role—avoid restating them without new impact.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if the opening is tighter, bullets start with outcomes, and channel-management points are de-duplicated from the earlier NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad intro with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, overseeing web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground impact: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable outcomes where missing: for email/social, include open rates, audience growth, engagement, production volume, or cost/time savings from the studio and analytics stack.
- Tighten phrasing: “Established NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting infrastructure.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; emphasize enterprise leadership, budget, governance, and platform modernization here.
- Video-program expansion also appears elsewhere; focus this item on building the studio and scaling organizational capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, editorial operations, and channel-building outcomes rather than broad ownership.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and function: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social, and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for NACo’s member audience.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video contribution with growth/consistency: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger operations bullet: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” is close to the Director role’s opening; avoid repeating “led/oversaw digital communications team.”
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager and footer project; use “established as recurring channel” to differentiate.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinct strengths rather than repeating broad digital/comms language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, less duplicative wording:
- Enterprise web and content strategy
- Editorial governance and publishing operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy content strategy
- Audience-centered planning and messaging
- Consider swapping one item for a more differentiated strength tied to recent work, e.g. “AI-enabled content discovery strategy” or “Digital transformation for mission-driven organizations.”
- Keep wording parallel: all noun phrases, no mixed styles like “audience-focused” vs. “leadership.”
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve “multi-channel communications” for experience bullets and let this section signal strategic specialization.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use “content strategy” or “stakeholder communications” instead.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize current differentiators and platform depth rather than repeating generic tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to grouped, higher-signal phrasing: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages • CMS modernization & front-end implementation • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” here unless the role targets hands-on developer work; “front-end implementation” is cleaner and less dated.
- Put Drupal first and keep AI-enabled search near the end as a differentiator tied to recent work.
- If space allows, add one impact cue: “supporting enterprise web modernization and scalable publishing workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies.
- Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages and coding tools are repeated in Technical + IT; this section should stay more selective.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capabilities and business use, not repeat every platform.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools and group them: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten the last items to outcome-oriented language: replace “SEO and performance analysis” with “SEO, UX and conversion/performance analysis.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive reporting dashboards • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid repeating the full tool stack here if it already appears in Technical + IT; Topline Skills should stay more strategic.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus several NACo bullets. Make it more specific to senior capability and delivery scope rather than listing basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery**
- Tighten and elevate the list to: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event production workflows • Post-production editing**
- If accurate, add scale/complexity language instead of generic terms, e.g. **multi-camera livestreams**, **in-house studio operations**, or **recurring advocacy video programming**
- Keep only 4–5 items; prioritize capabilities most relevant to the 2022–present leadership roles

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” partially duplicate Core Competencies’ **multimedia production and livestream operations**
- “Studio operations” and video production are already evidenced in NACo experience; avoid repeating identical phrasing elsewhere

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section. This item should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show depth and recency, e.g. “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, prioritize strongest/recent tools first and consider dropping the weakest/least-used platform if it wasn’t meaningfully used in recent roles.
- Use this section for platform names only; keep modernization/governance language in Topline Skills and impact in Work Experience.
- Optional tighter version: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages” if GitHub Pages is not central to target roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- “Drupal” is already strongly evidenced in recent experience; avoid repeating surrounding descriptors elsewhere unless adding new specificity here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should emphasize implementation tools not already covered elsewhere and modernize a few terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery; technical integrations: APIs, Google Tag Manager; serverless/automation: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider shortening “API integrations” to “REST/API integrations” if that reflects actual work; it sounds more specific.
- Replace separators with grouped labels to show structure and reduce the “laundry list” feel.
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “for Drupal-based campaign sites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating them verbatim in both places.
- GTM also overlaps conceptually with analytics infrastructure in recent roles, so keep this item tool-focused rather than impact-focused.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Reorder by strongest/relevant tools first: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp
- If space allows, add light functional grouping for clarity: Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/workflow: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If these tools were central in recent roles, consider replacing 1–2 lower-value names with a brief qualifier, e.g., “Airtable (workflow systems), Power Automate (process automation), Jira/Asana (cross-team planning)”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams are low-signal unless tied to operations; keep only if needed for ATS coverage.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it reads as a vendor list rather than a capability statement. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and tool-focused without repeating channel management claims.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability and consistency: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add one functional qualifier instead of more tools: campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation
- Optional rewrite: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | Campaign automation, newsletter distribution, audience segmentation

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience growth,” or “multi-channel communications” here; those are already covered in recent work experience and core competencies.
- Don’t expand this into outcomes unless you can tie them to a specific role; impact is better shown in the NACo entries.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item currently duplicates the “Topline Skills” analytics section almost exactly. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize methods and business use, not just a repeated tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics, Testing & Reporting
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • Executive dashboarding
- Put the strongest/most strategic tools first: lead with GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, then supporting tools.
- If space allows elsewhere, replace generic terms like “Dashboarding” with outcome-oriented language such as “KPI reporting” or “executive reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly redundant with “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider keeping tools here and reserving the topline section for capabilities only.
- “SEO” may overlap with broader digital strategy language; “SEO analysis” is more precise and technical.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal and useful scope, but it reads broadly and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make this item more foundational and specific, with 1–2 concrete outputs or scale indicators.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as an early-career build role: “Promoted across two digital positions to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten phrasing and emphasize execution: “Supported web, email, social and multimedia operations; improved publishing workflows; contributed to a major website refresh.”
- Add measurable detail if available: number of livestreams/events produced, cadence/reach of weekly video updates, size of team supported, or workflow/time savings.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported web, email, social and multimedia operations, contributed to a major website refresh, and produced recurring digital content including livestreams and weekly video updates. Also provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as launch/early production.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the innovation/program support angle and keep the podcast point as the clearest impact item.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and ownership: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program development and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Tighten the digital support language: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support organizational communications and member-facing initiatives.”
- If possible, add one concrete output or scale metric: number of projects supported, episodes produced, or programs/policy teams served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production and multimedia materials” phrasing already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership in digital strategy here; later positions already establish that progression.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item mixes software with capabilities and repeats multimedia themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, with the strongest, most current production capabilities implied by recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Creative & Production Tools
- Rewrite as: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator
- If you want to retain capability keywords, make them more specific and concise: Broadcast/livestream production • Podcast editing
- Consider moving non-tool phrases out of this technical list and into a recent role bullet if you can quantify them (e.g., studio launched, recurring video series, podcast created)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” overlaps with Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery.”
- “Podcast production” is already supported by older NACo experience; keep it only if space allows and newer skills don’t crowd it out.
